venue_now: COLM 2026: the page header reads 'Published as a conference paper at COLM 2026' (p.1); arXiv 2604.06996v3, 3 Aug 2026
what_it_is: The first study of self-preference bias in rubric-based evaluation, where a judge gives a binary verdict per criterion (p.1). On IFEval and LiveCodeBench, whose rubrics are programmatically verifiable, judges are more likely to mark a failed criterion as satisfied when the output is their own or their family's: 'can be more than 50% more likely' (p.1-2), controlling for instance difficulty and judge quality (p.2). Ensembling judges reduces the bias without removing it (p.1). On HealthBench, with subjective rubrics, the bias moves scores by up to 10 points (p.1).
domain: LLM-judge meta-evaluation (instruction following, code, medical chat)
evaluation: judge verdicts per rubric item against programmatic ground truth (p.1-2)
human_validation: n/a: the objective rubrics are checked programmatically (p.1)

for outputs that fail a rubric item, judges can be more than 50% more likely to mark it satisfied when the output is their own or their family's (p.1-2)
ensembling multiple judges mitigates the bias without fully eliminating it (p.1)
